meta.title: Platform terms and API feasibility audit for an NFL DFS forecasting workflow
meta.method: WebSearch (standard/extended) for discovery; WebFetch for primary documents; git clone of public GitHub repos for nflverse.

fetch_failures.error: CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403 (egress proxy policy)

meta.primary_access_note: Only github.com was reachable for primary reads (WebFetch of github.com pages, and anonymous git clone of nflverse/nflreadr @23f915a5be30415aeaa0c5c80cd23b2c69cda122 and nflverse/nflverse-data @a78da18ca93f167bd0a2af274df48f539fa4153c). Every non-GitHub vendor document (DraftKings, Fantasy Cruncher, NFL, Sportradar, SportsDataIO, Genius, ESPN/Disney, Sports Reference, RotoWire) was seen ONLY through search-engine result summaries and is labelled SNIPPET_ONLY. SNIPPET_ONLY quotes are text as the search tool returned it; they may be paraphrased or truncated and must be re-verified against the live page before being relied on.
meta.snippet_caveat: SNIPPET_ONLY quotes containing '...' or a parenthetical were assembled from search-tool summaries; they are not verified verbatim text.

api.finding: No official public developer API for DFS was found. The commonly used JSON endpoints (api.draftkings.com/draftgroups/v1/draftgroups/{id}/draftables, www.draftkings.com/lobby/getcontests) are undocumented and documented only by third parties, who state DraftKings does not intend public use. No DraftKings document sanctioning them was found.

evidence.quote: This is unofficial documentation for the Draft Kings API.
Draft Kings very much does NOT intend to have this API used by the public
To the best of my knowledge, DraftKings does not have an "official", well-documented public-facing API.
Instead, they have various HTTP endpoints that do not require authentication (so are "public" in this manner).
reverse-engineered endpoints exist on GitHub but break often and violate ToS (third-party claim, not DraftKings)

official_export.finding: Manual, logged-in CSV exports exist: (1) contest GameCenter 'Export Lineups to CSV' (documented by DraftKings' own Fair Play Commitment page); (2) salary file DKSalaries.csv via 'Export to CSV' on the draft-team/lineup page (described only by third parties); (3) 'Edit Entries' -> Download producing DKEntries.csv, plus CSV upload of new lineups and re-upload of edited entries (described only by third-party tool vendors). No DraftKings help article for (2) or (3) was retrieved.

authenticated_integration.finding: No public OAuth / API-key / developer program found. Third-party sources say documentation is shared only with contracted partners under NDA; partner arrangements exist (e.g. StreamNFT for Reignmakers) but none open to an individual forecaster were found.

automated_access_terms.finding: Prohibited. US Terms of Use bar automated means (scripts, third-party tools) to create/enter/withdraw contests or create/edit lineups, and bar harvesting bots/spiders/screen scrapers to obtain information on the site. The Fair Play Commitment says browser scripts or bots are prohibited. Optimizer tools must require multiple substantive user decisions. History: scripts briefly permitted for limited actions (2015), banned again January 2016 when DraftKings launched its own lineup tool. DraftKings has issued cease-and-desist letters over scraping (SuperLobby, 2015). Manual CSV export then manual CSV upload is the only route consistent with these terms.

evidence.quote: using automated means (including but not limited to scripts and third-party tools) to interact with the Website in any way, including, but not limited to: creating a contest, entering a contest, withdrawing from a contest, creating a lineup, and editing a lineup

using automated means (including but not limited to harvesting bots, robots, parser, spiders, or screen scrapers) to obtain, collect, or access any information on the Website or of any User for any purpose

Content providers are expressly prohibited from engaging in the distribution of pre-built lineups that require no substantive input from the user ... Lineup tools must require multiple, substantive, independent decisions by the users in order to generate a lineup
the use of automation tools such as browser scripts or bots is prohibited
DraftKings bans use of offsite scripts (2016 headline)
changed its terms to allow customers to use scripts to automate a short list of time-consuming behaviors (2015, superseded)
such a cease and desist request is standard procedure when it discovers what it believes to be a violation of its terms of use

redistribution_terms.finding: Third-party content providers may not distribute pre-built lineups needing no substantive user input. No clause specifically on redistributing exported salary/contest CSVs was retrieved; full TOU text not readable (DNS failure).

api.finding: No hosted API; data is published as public GitHub release assets (rds/csv/parquet) fetched over HTTPS by nflreadr (R) or by URL. Officially supported by the project, no key needed.

evidence.quote: This repository holds automated data releases for nflverse projects (i.e. all of the data powered/scraped via GitHub Actions).
You can download data hosted here with the `{nflreadr}` package, or manually download and access the [releases](https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data/releases) page.
Injuries data, accessed with `nflreadr::load_injuries()`
Depth chart data, accessed with `nflreadr::load_depth_charts()`

official_export.finding: Direct file downloads (csv/parquet/rds) from release pages, e.g. releases/download/depth_charts/depth_charts_{season}.rds.

evidence.quote: https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data/releases/download/depth_charts/depth_charts_{seasons}.rds

scheduled_delivery.finding: Pull-only on a published cron cadence (no push). Injuries: daily 07:00 UTC Sep-Feb. Rosters and depth charts: daily 07:00 UTC year-round. Schedules: every 5 minutes in season. PBP/player stats: nightly 09:00 UTC plus game-window runs; raw pbp every 15 min; stat corrections Wed 02:00 UTC. PFR snap counts/advstats and FTN charting: every 6 h in season. Note: workflows.md is labelled internal and dated 16 Sep 2026.

evidence.quote: [Injury Data](https://nflreadr.nflverse.com/articles/dictionary_injuries.html) updates every day at 7AM UTC throughout the season.
[Depth Charts](https://nflreadr.nflverse.com/articles/dictionary_depth_charts.html) update every day at 7AM UTC throughout the year.
[Roster data](https://nflreadr.nflverse.com/reference/load_rosters.html) updates every day at 7AM UTC.
[Game/Schedule data](https://nflreadr.nflverse.com/reference/load_schedules.html) updates very 5 minutes during the season.

[Snap Count data](https://nflreadr.nflverse.com/reference/load_snap_counts.html) updates every day at 0, 6, 12, 18 UTC during the season. The actual availability of new data depends on the update schedule of PFR.

In all cases, it is recommended to update the data again during the night from Wednesday to Thursday in order to also receive the stat corrections that the NFL will incorporate from Monday to Wednesday at the latest.

cron:  '0 7 * 1,2,9,10,11,12 *'  (update_injuries.yaml)

automated_access_terms.finding: Automated download is the intended use (nflreadr is a programmatic loader). However, nflverse itself scrapes/derives from third parties: depth charts switched from NFL Data Exchange to ESPN (2025); snap counts/advstats/combine/draft from Pro Football Reference; participation and charting from FTN; injuries 'collected from an API' (source not named); IDs keyed on NFL GSIS. Upstream terms (ESPN/Disney, Sports Reference, NFL) therefore still bind the underlying data.

redistribution_terms.finding: Split licensing. nflreadr code: MIT. nflverse-data repository: CC BY 4.0 (attribution). But nflreadr states NFL data belong to their owners and are governed by their terms -- so CC BY on the repo does not clear upstream rights. FTN charting and 2023+ participation: CC-BY-SA 4.0 with mandatory attribution 'FTN Data via nflverse'. No per-dataset licence statement found for injuries, rosters, depth charts, schedules or player stats beyond the repo licence.

evidence.quote: The R code for this package is released as open source under the [MIT License](https://nflreadr.nflverse.com/LICENSE.html). NFL data accessed by this package belong to their respective owners, and are governed by their terms of use.

api.finding: No official public NFL developer API found. Official data is distributed by licence: Genius Sports is the exclusive distributor of official play-by-play, Next Gen Stats and the betting data feed (2021; extended 2023 through 2027-28; expanded 2025 through the 2029 season). Sportradar held the exclusive statistics distribution role from 2015 and a betting-data deal in 2020; no source explicitly states its termination (Genius displacing it is an inference).
